synopsis: The booklet treats latency as a first-order stopping-distance contributor: at 5–15 km/h it can account for half or more of stopping distance, and milliseconds in sensing, networking, decision and actuation change the stopping point [f144, f13659, f4346]. The reviewed 2022 DIS and ISO 21815-3:2023 distance structures include detection, determination and action, physical stopping and residual safety distance; a practical engineering model adds speed multiplied by detection, decision and actuation times to braking distance, machine-envelope offset and margin, but is not a verbatim ISO equation [f2419, f7007, f7010]. In the worked 40 t example at 15 km/h on a 10% downgrade with 1.0 s delay, stopping takes about 8.5 m and 1 m clearance raises minimum detection range to 9.5 m before sensor-error allowance; the US mining rule's assumed 2.0 s delay alone contributes 8.3 m at that speed [f13656, f13658]. Validation should timestamp a known object event through detection, confirmation, risk decision, brake request, interface receipt, actuator response and measurable deceleration, test the automated rather than merely pedal brake path, and include end-to-end integration latency when using the specified third-party J1939 interface [f6159, f6142, f8198]. When the prototype arrives in mid-2027, correlation measurements on representative variants should precede the full scenario matrix, establishing latency, detection range, brake-command timing, stopping dynamics, repeatability and model error [f744, f13512]. A coverage gap remains because the seven sensor questions omitted synchronization and latency, so realistic individual sensor values do not guarantee a working braking function; detector operating-point metrics also omit downstream braking logic and timing, while combined mining-document delays must not be interpreted as measured human reaction-time distributions [f5092, f6981, f3327].

Both require initial latency, range and brake-timing measurements before large scenario sweeps.
